title: Acting and its effect on her singing
summary: She credits her film directors and acting as part of being a storyteller.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Did you feel at any point that your background in theater and on stage became a part of the stage persona and presence that you have?

All of it contributes to the work that I have, experience as an actress or an actor. I don't mind being called an actor. Michael Romer, who was my first serious film, dramatic film, and he made me know, he made me think that I was really a talented and a great actress, and I took his direction, and then I had a chance to make "For Love of Ivy," and I had another great director, Danny Mann, who would give me a direction. I was fortunate. Those are the only two really films I made. "For Love of Ivy." "Nothing But A Man" and "For Love of Ivy." Well, just like Triptic helped me as a singer and as an actress, acting taught me a lot about what singing was all about and the stage. I'm a storyteller. I use words and sound and music and I know how to act out things on the stage. I'm really a ham.
